sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Settings template for the app
sections.what: Lists the settings the app reads, grouped by purpose: where the database lives, keys for AI services, optional paid map and translation keys, environment mode, and log detail. The owner fills these in to tell the app which services to use.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps secret keys out of the program code so the same program can run with different keys.
sections.watch_out: Never place real keys in this template, because it is meant to be shared and copied.

summary: A template that lists every setting the app reads from a file named .env, with placeholder values and short comments.
purpose: Tells the owner which settings exist, which ones are required, and which ones are optional.
why: The setup script copies this file to .env, so the owner only has to fill in the values.
how: Copy the file to .env, replace the placeholder keys, leave optional keys blank if they are not used, and then run setup or the app.
inputs: The owner's values for database address, AI service keys, optional map and translation keys, environment mode, and log detail.
outputs: Nothing directly. The app reads these values when it starts.
risks: Placeholder keys must be replaced or AI calls will fail. Real keys must never be shared or committed to version control. The comment on the ENVIRONMENT line sits on the same line as its value, which some .env readers may treat as part of the value.
debug: If a setting seems ignored, check the spelling of the name and confirm that the .env file, not this template, is the file being edited. The database message printed by init shows which database address is in use.
